## Qualified and published — 2026-10-08

The ten-case source table and source-derived fixtures preserve valid layouts and retain instructions for ambiguous placement. No safe generic relocation mapping was demonstrated, so no relocation action or repair screen was implemented; repair-only criteria are not applicable, not falsely claimed passed. Concrete coverage defects were separately fixed and qualified under #520/#521/#522/#523. #508 integration and #507 scope name this exact disposition.

Product integration `e6645cb5ea5ae3c7f699390a74b22d098fbeb7fb` and [retained proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-save-repair-cases) are published on next `bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3`; ES integration is `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. The independent delta audit (#507), assembled firmware inclusion/public adoption (#508), affected device builds and release gates remain separate. #519 must pass before the owner's next handheld update transfer/reboot. No personal cloud or physical action was part of this qualification.

The sections below retain the problem, requirement and investigation history; this status supersedes their earlier in-progress observations.

## Purpose and placement

M7.P5 implementation work under #510's settled post-rclone setup design (D-CLOUD-178). Identify concrete supported game-save, save-state and screenshot placement problems, then deliver only the bounded, explicitly confirmed repairs that the evidence supports. This is the active implementation task before #508 final integration and #507's frozen delta audit; it is not another request for the owner to choose the overall design.

## Maintainer request — 2026-10-08

> I think we arrived at a good solution for this. I want to make sure everything we had is well documented, put into issues, and that we have a clear implementation path around using our project management methodology.
>
> I feel like we arrived at a good solution that relied on post-rclone remote setup. At the time, verification, directory creation, and user actions could live, so someone could help tidy up certain elements while we provide documentation for how to handle more data-intensive operations.
>
> This would also mean refactoring and redoing what we had done around the initial upgrade path, but I'm fine manually aligning myself with our new framework and directory structure. I can also revert the changes we made in Dropbox and then simply retitle the directory on my end.

## What exists today

The qualified local validator, independent folder settings, explicit selected-category creation and local instructions are implemented in distribution `6f89bc7cecee5972909828103689e2c7c0711c30` and ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. See `docs/pixelelated/cloud-folder-flow-review.md` and its CF01–CF15 evidence. No generic save-file relocation API exists and no concrete safe repair mapping has been demonstrated. Public ROCKNIX's progress allowlist deliberately supports standalone emulator layouts and save extensions outside `savefiles`; those are not automatically misplaced. Screenshots and save states are not inherently small.

## Implementation order

1. Inspect the pinned public ROCKNIX 20261001 config/filter and actual emulator save writers against the qualified validator. Produce a case table: exact observed layout, why it is wrong, supported destination and consumer, affected class, detection evidence, and supported/unsupported disposition. Use synthetic examples derived from those writers, not the owner's Dropbox layout. Valid standalone layouts must remain valid. Do not search outside selected roots to invent a case.
2. For each demonstrably safe case, define a read-only plan bound to remote/configuration/selected root and file identity: exact source/destination, file count and bytes, explicit size/transport limits, verification cost, source-retention and collision behavior. Reuse proven classifiers/readers; do not revive the removed whole-folder migration engine. Unknown, ambiguous, oversized or unsupported cases lead to instructions.
3. Add the separate preview/confirmation/action and recheck only for supported cases. Preserve conflicting versions and originals until the stated verification/retention contract is met; no implicit newest-wins, overwrite, deletion, settings-archive or ROM/BIOS/game-content move. Checking, connecting, selecting a path, and opening instructions do not grant repair consent. Failed/stale/interrupted actions must preserve recoverable files and report the actual outcome.
4. Prove detection/refusal, consent and any supported repair on synthetic host and GENERIC_X64 fixtures; update the canonical flow plus reviewed indexed happy/error/cancel/retry frames with the source. Integrate its result through #508 and include it in #507's frozen audit payload.

If source investigation finds no safe automatic case, record that finding with the case table and consumer evidence; retain instructions for those cases. Do not invent a blanket repair or tick an unimplemented repair as passed. A discovered defect in the supported layout/validator is a tracked fix, not an excuse to defer it. Any proposal to omit a demonstrated, requested repair must be explicitly reflected in #510 and M7, not silently dropped from the release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A source-cited case table separates supported repairs, valid layouts and unsupported/ambiguous findings; synthetic fixtures reproduce each classification, including legitimate standalone-emulator saves.
- [x] Every supported repair has an exact plan/consent/size/transport/source-retention/collision contract and fixture; if none is supportable, the evidence-backed disposition is explicit in #510, the flow reference and M7, with no claimed repair completion.
- [x] For every implemented repair, failing controls prove stale-plan refusal, preservation of conflicting versions/originals, bounded transfer/verification costs, cancellation/retry safety and exclusion of ROMs, BIOS, settings archives, game content and unknown files. Before/after inventories and hashes show unselected files unchanged.
- [x] For every implemented repair, actual VM frames and operation receipts prove separate preview/confirmation, decline/no-op, interruption/failure, retry, result and recheck; canonical IA/diagram/evidence index match the source, with EN/FR and both panel layouts reviewed for affected content. If no repair case is supportable, record the evidence-backed no-action disposition and reuse unchanged instruction-flow proof explicitly; do not require or fabricate repair screens.
- [x] #508's integration manifest and #507's frozen scope name the final supported implementation or evidence-backed instructions-only disposition; no new build or release claim relies on an unproved repair.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: source-derived synthetic fixtures and disposable GENERIC_X64 guests can prove these behaviors. No device action, personal-cloud inventory or Dropbox credentials are needed. Retain compact records; retire scratch when its named proof is complete.

## Owner-managed alignment and separate private review

The owner reports manually resetting the experimental cloud state and has requested read-only verification plus a later one-time residue review. #516 owns that private operational task, outside M7. Exact account history, timestamps, paths and object inventory remain restricted locally; the tracker records redacted conclusions only.

The report is not verified transfer integrity and does not establish reset device pointers. A later device test uses the new post-connection flow and named action authority; it does not resume the retired automatic migration. No move, deletion, sync or credential export is authorized by the read-only review. Public ROCKNIX/clean qualification uses independent synthetic fixtures and does not wait for personal cleanup.

## Verification lessons carried forward from #517

D-CLOUD-181 and `docs/cloud-save-integrity.md` apply to this task's existing synthetic controls: retain complete manifests (including benign credential-like filename substrings), bind before/after identities, refuse partial listings/failed reads/stale inputs, and distinguish byte equality from container structure and game/core compatibility. A provider can hash an already-damaged file correctly. Use `tools/cloud-save-integrity` where its supported formats/provider contract fit; never claim that it validates unknown core payloads.

These are additions to fixture design and repair verification, not a requirement to download a library during CHECK CLOUD FOLDERS. Personal inventories are not fixtures. Preserve the existing explicit byte/time/transport limits and source-retention contract.


## Active source-coverage fix — #520

#520 is a child of #515 and must qualify before #508 integration and #507 scope freeze. Full packaged writer chains confirm ordinary PPSSPP savedata, DuckStation memory cards and standalone Mupen64Plus save states can be omitted by current save rules or misclassified as ROM content. Correct coverage in place, including backup/restore, content copy/match/list/count and bounded validator consumers; preserve supported existing layouts. Synthetic old-source failure and fixed-source byte-preservation controls plus affected actual VM presentation proof are in progress. This is not consent to relocate saves or clean private clouds.

Source investigation also identified an old unpublished-fork wrapper defect. Public ROCKNIX did not create that wrapper, and current selected-root names alone cannot establish its provenance or a unique safe destination. Keep that case explicitly separate from valid layouts and confirmed coverage bugs; source evidence will determine its final repair disposition.


## Additional confirmed writer gap — #521

Child #521 qualifies DuckStation default screenshot placement. The exact packaged screenshot action/writer and shipped VM/H700 seeds resolve ordinary captures outside the saves tree. Correct new default capture placement while preserving explicit custom paths and all historical captures; source-derived launcher controls and target-runtime proof accompany the change. This is a separate scoped fix before #508/#507, not a general reorganization feature or permission to move personal files.


## DuckStation runtime prerequisite — #522

Actual GENERIC_X64 proof for #521 found the exact pinned AppImage installed mode0644; direct execution refuses with126. #522 fixes explicit package executable mode and proves original/fixed install behavior plus real target entrypoint execution. It precedes #521 screenshot runtime acceptance. Preserve the source/cache bytes and persistent saves; no guest-only chmod is a product fix. Include this input in #508 integration and #507 scope.


## Qualification update — 2026-10-08

#520 source coverage is qualified locally at `1ee8e5199da0bc02e6aa4ebff94b951f5e8b4804`: 39 focused controls, 21 content regressions, 30 validator regressions and nine actual-image BusyBox controls pass. The affected VM UI packet has ten reviewed frames, one retained rejected fixture frame and no pending #520 UI case; root verified all 194 sealed files and unchanged content/configuration witnesses. Publication/inclusion still belongs to #508.

#521/#522 local commit `dda2a04aaf411b8bc13aedf5ce44ff33ce4b3d3a` passes 31 host controls against four original-source failures. Actual guest proof confirms executable permission repair, preserved custom/history state and the helper behavior. The real application loader then exposed #523: missing `libcom_err.so.2`. A complete 121-ELF/plugin scan found this sole unresolved SONAME. Qualify the target-built dependency and actual rendered capture before claiming #521 runtime completion. No host-library substitution, personal cloud or physical action is involved.

Current order: finish #523 and #521 runtime proof, reconcile #515's finite instructions-only relocation disposition, integrate #508, freeze/audit #507, then assembled GENERIC_X64 clean/public adoption and affected H700 followed by SM8550 builds. No external audit or new firmware build has started. #519 separately gates the owner's next handheld update transfer/reboot; old consumers and active fallback configs require controlled alignment and residue disposition first.
